newsitem.title: USA: Agreement elusive on US futures trade reform - Lugar.
newsitem.headline: Agreement elusive on US futures trade reform - Lugar.

text.p: The attempt to modernize the basic U.S. law regulating futures trading is rife with disagreement, Senate Agriculture Committee chairman Richard Lugar said Tuesday.
Lugar, Indiana Republican, said he was encouraging the factions to negotiate but "I have no idea" if a consensus would emerge in the near future.

"There is considerable division among the (commodity) exchanges," Lugar said in an interview. In addition, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, which regulates the futures industry, has a different position than the exchanges.

Nor has the Treasury Department taken a definitive position on refining the so-called Treasury amendment, Lugar said. The provision is one of the major issues in updating the Commodity Exchange Act. It was written in the 1970s to exempt interbank foreign exchange transactions from CFTC regulation but there have been many attempts to widen the exemption.
A Lugar aide described work on the reforms as "tedious" and said no bill-drafting session was expected in the committee in the near term.

Other major issues were defining the scope of federal regulation of derivatives and proposals to create "professionals-only" commodity markets for sophisticated and well-financed investors that would have less regulatory oversight than other markets.
Federal agencies have disagreed over the appropriate parameters for "pro markets" and commodity exchanges have proposed far more freedom for the markets than regulators favor.
